stem: A Fycompa prescription is five months old and has three prior refills. Select all supported statements.

choices.text: The federal six-month issue-date clock remains relevant.
The prescription can be refilled indefinitely if seizure control is stable.
Covered Schedule III dispensing is reported to MassPAT.
Fycompa is noncontrolled because it is an antiseizure drug.
A new prescription is required after every fill because it is Schedule II.

explanation.core_reasoning: Apply each proposition independently. A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner. Covered pharmacies report dispensing of Schedule II through V controlled substances and DPH-designated additional drugs, including gabapentin, to the Massachusetts PMP under the current submission standard. perampanel (Fycompa) is used for treatment of partial-onset seizures and primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures. It is federal Schedule III and Massachusetts Schedule III; its legal consequence in this scenario follows the cited schedule-specific rule.

choice_analysis.B: This statement imports Schedule II prescriptions may not be refilled without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.
choice_analysis.C: The proposition 'Covered Schedule III dispensing is reported to MassPAT.' is supported by Massachusetts pharmacy MassPAT dispensing-data reporting: Covered pharmacies report dispensing of Schedule II through V controlled substances and DPH-designated additional drugs, including gabapentin, to the Massachusetts PMP under the current submission standard.
choice_analysis.D: This statement imports Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription-drug status without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.
choice_analysis.E: This statement imports Schedule II partial fill caused by pharmacy inability without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.
